chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

Indeed, for God, Exalted and Mighty, are three unique things to respect: His Book, which is His Light and Wisdom; His House, which He established as the Qiblah for people, and God will not accept from anyone a face turned towards any other direction; and the Household of your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.حَرَمَاتٍ: Sacred things or things to be respected

ai.seo_question: What are the three unique things God has made sacred according to this hadith from Ibn Abbas?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the triad of divine reverence by elevating the Ahl al-Bayt to the same ontological status as the Quran and the Kaaba, a key concept in Shia theology known as 'Tathir'. This narration underscores the inseparable link between the Book and its interpreters, suggesting that just as the Kaaba is the focal point of physical worship, the Ahl al-Bayt are the focal point of spiritual guidance and understanding of divine wisdom.
